articles.title: E. coli found again in Curitiba tap water, residents of Agua Verde ask the utility for answers
articles.description: Tests in the Agua Verde district found the same E. coli strain for the second time in 16 days. About 200 households report cloudy, foul-smelling water and the state water company has issued a boil notice.

articles.title: Denmark cuts the residency needed for citizenship to six years for working residents
articles.description: Parliament approved a shorter path to Danish citizenship. Residents with a full-time job, Danish language level and no benefit claims can apply after six years instead of nine, starting next spring.

articles.title: Denmark sets a minimum bank balance for people who invite visitors on a visa
articles.description: Hosts in Denmark who sponsor a family visit must now show a minimum balance on their account for the 90 days before the application.

articles.title: European gas prices fall as mild weather cuts heating demand
articles.description: Benchmark gas prices in Europe dropped for a third week as mild temperatures reduced heating demand and storage stayed above 90 percent.

articles.title: Copenhagen rental market stalls and the personal fallout is often severe
articles.description: Tenants in Copenhagen cannot move because there is nothing to move to, and landlords report record queues for every flat. Housing associations describe long waiting lists.

articles.title: Revolutionary Guard says two oil tankers exploded after hitting sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz; heating oil and gas prices in Europe jump
articles.description: Two tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Traders expect higher fuel and heating prices across Europe this winter.

articles.title: US families sue Microsoft and OpenAI, warning of a "grave danger" from AI chatbots
articles.description: A group of families filed a lawsuit in a federal court in California claiming that AI chatbots pose a grave danger to children and seeking damages.

articles.title: Korean actress sues a studio over AI face-swap videos using her likeness
articles.description: The actress filed a lawsuit in Seoul saying a video studio used AI to copy her face without consent.

articles.title: Black bean prices rise in Curitiba markets, feijao reaches 9 reais a kilo
articles.description: Prices of black beans and rice rose in Curitiba open markets this week while sugar prices declined slightly.

articles.title: This EU country has the cheapest housing for young buyers, but rent still takes almost half of income
articles.description: A new survey ranks EU countries by home affordability. Rent in the cheapest one still eats nearly half of a young renter's pay.

articles.title: Peruvian media groups in Arequipa sign a declaration on AI-generated news
articles.description: Regional editors meeting in Arequipa signed a declaration asking that AI use in newsrooms be disclosed to readers.

articles.title: Two big orders in Curitiba: protest rallies need police notice, landlords must not evict tenants on short notice
articles.description: The city issued two orders. Organisers of protests must inform the police beforehand, and landlords are barred from forcing tenants out with less than 30 days notice.

articles.title: Tears from a tenant after drugs found in her flat: "If I had known, he would have been out"
articles.description: A Copenhagen housing association is evicting a tenant after police found drugs in the flat she had sublet. She says she knew nothing and the case goes to court.

articles.title: Training AI models keeps consuming more energy, French researchers find
articles.description: A study from a French research institute measured the electricity used by training runs over five years and found steady growth.

articles.title: Rail service resumes between Helsinki Central and Pasila after a signal fault
articles.description: Trains between Helsinki Central and Pasila are running again after a signal fault earlier in the day caused delays.

articles.title: Copenhagen introduces a record tourist tax from 2027
articles.description: The city council voted for a tourist tax on every hotel night, among the highest in Europe.

articles.title: Why Copenhagen will soon charge the highest tourist tax in Europe
articles.description: Hotels warn that the new levy will push nightly prices up for visitors, while the city says it will fund harbour cleanup.

articles.title: Who is liable when an AI agent causes harm? Singapore law school seminar covers four legal puzzles
articles.description: A seminar at a Singapore law school discussed liability, contracts, privacy and evidence when AI agents act for users.

articles.title: EU nations to unveil a deal with Kenya for a migrant return hub
articles.description: Several EU governments will present an agreement to send rejected asylum seekers to a processing hub in Kenya.

articles.title: Contract nurses in Goias state to get health insurance cover
articles.description: Health workers on contract with the state health service will be added to the public insurance scheme next year.

articles.title: Opinion: using AI to spread fakes
articles.description: A columnist argues that AI tools make disinformation cheaper to produce and harder to trace.

articles.title: Utility deploys 60 MWh of battery storage across Sao Paulo
articles.description: The power utility installed battery storage at substations across Sao Paulo to ease evening peaks.

articles.title: Heavy rain and cold nights forecast for Minas Gerais this week
articles.description: Forecasters expect rain in the state with cooler nights through the weekend.

articles.title: Spain fail to keep their record as England end the unbeaten run in the Nations League
articles.description: England beat Spain in the Nations League while Italy crashed out of the competition.

articles.title: Apple launches an AI health research app to study how people look for medical advice
articles.description: The research app will study how users search for health information and talk to AI about it.

articles.title: Opinion: protect creators whose work trains AI without permission
articles.description: A columnist calls for stronger protections for writers and artists whose work is used to train AI models.

articles.title: Hong Kong promises a new cybersecurity law to defend against AI risks
articles.description: The government said a new cybersecurity law will address risks from AI and cross-border attacks.

articles.title: Simpler visas, firmer checks: how Brazil is rebuilding its e-visa system
articles.description: Brazil's foreign ministry is rebuilding its e-visa platform with faster approvals and stricter document checks.

articles.title: The world's happiest passports: beyond visa-free travel, what matters most
articles.description: A ranking looks at which passports give holders the best quality of life as well as easy travel.

articles.title: International overview 2026: the most important AI news of week 46
articles.description: A weekly digest of AI product launches, funding rounds and policy news from around the world.

articles.title: Business Brief: five files to follow this week
articles.description: A round-up of the corporate and economic stories to watch in the coming days.

articles.title: US government proposes one-sentence change to USCIS rules for L-1 visa holders
articles.description: A proposed one-line change in the rules would alter how long intra-company transferees can stay.

articles.title: Electricity and gas get more expensive: Essen utility announces price increases
articles.description: The municipal utility will raise electricity and gas prices from January.

articles.title: National demonstration on 23 November: Antwerp De Lijn network will be heavily disrupted
articles.description: Trams and buses in Antwerp will run a reduced service during a national demonstration.
